discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (2D materials, moire quantum matter)
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted in 2011 that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees would flatten the electronic bands, so that interactions would dominate over kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group built these devices by controlled tear-and-stack fabrication and found correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity, tunable with a gate voltage. Many groups worldwide have since reproduced the results, which is the test I care most about. The work turned a single geometric parameter, the twist angle, into a control knob for strongly correlated physics. It launched the field of moire quantum matter, which now includes correlated magnetism, Chern insulators and the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect. Few discoveries have so directly shown how nanoscale fabrication can create new phases of matter on demand.
